# language: en
@FR-012
Feature: Request annual leave
  As an employee
  I want to request annual leave from the people team
  So that my time off is agreed before I plan around it

  Leave requests are checked against the employee's remaining allowance. A
  request that overlaps a team blackout period needs the manager's sign-off.

  Background:
    Given an employee with 12 days of annual leave remaining

  Scenario: Approve a request within the allowance
    When the employee requests 5 days of leave starting on 3 November
    Then the request is approved under the leave policy
    And the employee has 7 days of annual leave remaining

  Scenario: Refuse a request that exceeds the allowance
    When the employee requests 15 days of leave
    Then the request is refused because it exceeds the remaining allowance
    And the employee still has 12 days of annual leave remaining

  Scenario: Hold a request that overlaps a blackout period
    Given the team has a blackout period from 15 to 19 December
    When the employee requests 2 days of leave starting on 18 December
    Then the request waits for the manager's sign-off

  Scenario: Pro-rate the allowance of a new starter
    Given a new starter who joined on 1 October and is still in onboarding
    When the people team calculates the new starter's allowance
    Then the new starter has 6 days of annual leave for the rest of the year

@dk:context=shipping @dk:persona=example-persona @dk:mission=mission-alpha @dk:adr=0001 @FR-003
Feature: Book a consignment
  As a shipper
  I want to book cargo onto a sailing
  So that my goods travel on a confirmed slot

  A booking reserves space on one sailing for one consignment. Bookings that
  exceed the sailing's remaining capacity are refused, and the shipper sees why.

  Background:
    Given a sailing from Rotterdam to Felixstowe with 40 TEU remaining

  Rule: A booking within capacity is confirmed

    @smoke
    Scenario: Book cargo that fits
      Given a consignment of 12 TEU
      When the shipper books the consignment onto the sailing
      Then the booking is confirmed
      And the sailing has 28 TEU remaining

    Scenario: Attach a packing list to a confirmed booking
      Given a confirmed booking for a consignment of 2 TEU
      When the shipper attaches the packing list:
        """json
        { "lines": [{ "sku": "A-1", "qty": 10 }, { "sku": "B-2", "qty": 4 }] }
        """
      Then the booking shows 2 packing-list lines

  Rule: A booking over capacity is refused

    Scenario Outline: Refuse cargo that does not fit
      Given a consignment of <size> TEU
      When the shipper books the consignment onto the sailing
      Then the booking is refused with reason "<reason>"

      @edge
      Examples: Over capacity
        | size | reason             |
        | 41   | insufficient space |
        | 120  | insufficient space |

    Scenario: Refused bookings state the remaining capacity
      Given these consignments are already booked:
        | consignment | size |
        | C-100       | 30   |
        | C-101       | 8    |
      When the shipper books a consignment of 5 TEU onto the sailing
      Then the booking is refused with reason "insufficient space"
      And the refusal states that 2 TEU remain

# language: en
@dk:context=shipping @dk:persona=example-persona @dk:adr=0001 @FR-004
Feature: Declare a consignment to customs
  As a shipper
  I want to declare my cargo to customs before it sails
  So that the consignment clears the border without being held

  Every consignment that crosses a customs border needs a declaration lodged
  before the sailing's cut-off. The declared value sets the duty owed, and an
  insured consignment names the marine policy that covers it.

  Background:
    Given a booked consignment from Rotterdam to Felixstowe
    And the customs cut-off is 24 hours before the sailing departs
    And goods with a declared value under 150 EUR are relieved of duty

  Rule: Duty follows the declared value and the commodity's duty rate

    Scenario Outline: Calculate the duty owed on a declaration
      Given the cargo is declared under a commodity code with a duty rate of <rate>%
      And its declared value is <value> EUR
      When the shipper lodges the declaration before the cut-off
      Then the declaration is accepted
      And the duty owed is <duty> EUR

      Examples: Dutiable goods
        | rate | value | duty |
        | 6    | 10000 | 600  |
        | 0    | 25000 | 0    |

      @edge
      Examples: Below the relief threshold
        | rate | value | duty |
        | 6    | 120   | 0    |

  Rule: A declaration carries the evidence customs asks for

    Scenario: Lodge a declaration for an insured consignment
      Given the consignment is insured under a marine cargo policy
      When the shipper lodges this declaration:
        """xml
        <declaration consignment="C-100">
          <goods code="6912.00" value="10000" currency="EUR"/>
          <insurance policy="MC-2026-0412"/>
        </declaration>
        """
      Then the declaration is accepted
      And the declaration records the policy reference "MC-2026-0412"

    Scenario: Hold a declaration lodged after the cut-off
      Given the customs cut-off has passed
      When the shipper lodges the declaration
      Then the declaration is held for manual review
      And the freight invoice carries a late-lodgement surcharge

# language: en
@wip @dk:context=shipping
Feature: Track a consignment in transit
  As a shipper
  I want to see where my consignment is on its voyage
  So that I can tell the consignee when to expect it

  Tracking is still being designed: these scenarios record the milestones
  agreed so far, and the carrier event feed they depend on is not live yet.

  Scenario: Report the latest milestone
    Given a consignment loaded onto a sailing from Rotterdam to Felixstowe
    When the vessel departs Rotterdam
    Then the consignment is reported as in transit

  Scenario: Report a delay against the planned arrival
    Given a consignment in transit with a planned arrival on 14 November
    When the carrier reports a revised arrival on 16 November
    Then the consignment is reported as delayed by 2 days

Feature: Set up Spec Kitty in a repository
  As a developer adopting Spec Kitty
  I want `spec-kitty init` to set up my project without touching my git history
  So that I can add Spec Kitty to a new or existing repository, and re-run it to repair a damaged setup

  Scenario: Re-running init repairs a missing agent skill folder and keeps the rest of the project as it was
    Given a project already set up with Spec Kitty for the agents "claude,codex"
    And the folder ".claude/skills" has been deleted
    And the folder ".agents/skills" is present
    And the file ".kittify/config.yaml" is present
    When I run "spec-kitty init --non-interactive --ai claude,codex"
    Then the command succeeds
    And the folder ".claude/skills" exists
    And the folder ".claude/skills" is not empty
    And the folder ".agents/skills" is unchanged
    And the file ".kittify/config.yaml" is unchanged

  Scenario: Setting up a new project inside an existing repository leaves its git history alone
    Given an existing git repository with commit history
    And the repository has at least one commit
    When I run "spec-kitty init app --non-interactive --ai claude"
    Then the command succeeds
    And the folder "app/.kittify" exists
    And the folder "app/.claude" exists
    And no ".git" folder exists in "app"
    And the repository HEAD is unchanged
    And the repository has no new commits
